newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Goh calls for review of Singapore's competitiveness.
newsitem.headline: Goh calls for review of Singapore's competitiveness.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong has called for a review of the city-state's economic competitiveness after the recent decline in economic growth, especially in the electronics sector.

The Strait Times newspaper reported on Tuesday that Goh wants the review to study if the Singapore dollar is too strong, if rentals are too high and how other countries around the region are catching up with Singapore.

"We have been having it good for too long. Some people may think miracles happen all the time," Goh was quoted by the paper as telling reporters in Manila after attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
The government has said that Singapore's economy will grow by six percent for the year as a whole.
The economy had expanded by 11.4 percent in the first quarter, but growth slowed to 7.5 percent in the second and to 3.2 percent in the third.
The Ministry of Trade and Industry said the economy will grow by 2.6 percent year-on-year in the fourth quarter.
Goh said the government is not too worried about the slowdown. The economic fundamentals remained good and there should be an upturn in the economy in 1997, he said.
